toasting-spices.name: קליית תבלינים
reasons: The Cumin source only lists substituted (methoxy/ethoxy) pyrazines among aroma compounds of toasted cumin; it does not say they are formed by toasting, absent from raw cumin, or roast and nutty smelling. These alkoxypyrazines are typically natural green and earthy compounds. The dek, paragraph 2, a fact, the quiz answer and the cumin relation all rest on this claim, so fixing it would mean a rewrite.
Garam masala being toasted before grinding, and briefly toasting already-ground blends, are not in any listed source (Tempering page mentions only dry-roasting whole spices).

kanafeh.name: כנאפה
reasons: Headline, dek and a fact present 'no cheese kanafeh before the 19th century' as settled fact, but the cited Wikipedia page says the 13th-century Maghreb-Andalus cookbook has knafeh recipes layered with fresh cheese; the claim is only Mary Isin's view and the whole angle would need rewriting.
Body juxtaposes the 13th-century pancake with Isin's claim without mentioning the cheese layering, which misleads.
